title: Finite reduction of adic completion
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme, $\Lambda$ a commutative Noetherian ring, $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ a finitely generated ideal, $P_n=\Lambda/I^n$ for $n\geq1$, and $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$ satisfy [def-weil-pbc-complete-coefficient-datum]. Thus $\Lambda/I$ is additive torsion and every $P_n$ in degree zero is perfect over $\Lambda$. All coefficient sheaves in this statement are constant: write $\Lambda_X$ and $(P_n)_X$, and put $K_n=K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}(P_n)_X$. Regard the reductions as $\Lambda_X$-objects by restriction of scalars. Compute their strict reduction tower using one K-flat representative of $K$ [def-weil-derived-tensor], and let $L=R\lim_n K_n$ be its total right derived inverse limit [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], with canonical evaluation $p_a:L\to K_a$.

For every $a\geq1$, the adjoint of $p_a$ under derived extension and restriction of scalars [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction, lem-pc-derived-adjoint-functors] is a functorial isomorphism in $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},P_a)$:
$$L\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}(P_a)_X\xrightarrow{\sim}K_a.$$
No derived completeness hypothesis on $K$ is imposed.

proof.text: Choose a K-flat representative $C$ of $K$, with flat terms, using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Use the Koszul complexes $Q_m$ and strict transitions of [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-koszul-completion]. By [lemma-weil-pbc-koszul-quotient-limit], their quotient augmentations induce a natural isomorphism $c_K:R\lim_m(C\otimes(Q_m)_X)\to L$. This comparison is induced by the strict maps, not an arbitrary isomorphism of vertices. The hypotheses are precisely the constant-coefficient Noetherian datum in the statement.

source.place: Proof, first sentence: replace the quotient tower by the Koszul tower

proof.text: Fix $a$. Choose a bounded finite-projective ring complex representing $P_a$ by [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. Its derived isomorphism to $P_a[0]$ is represented by a chain map by [lem-pc-ring-derived-map-representative], applied in the category of $\Lambda$-modules; this map is a quasi-isomorphism since it induces the given isomorphism on cohomology. Constant presheaves preserve this quasi-isomorphism termwise, and exact sheafification [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact] preserves it. Thus the coefficient package [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package] gives a bounded finite-projective resolution $E^\bullet\to(P_a)_X$, whose terms are retracts of finite sums of $\Lambda_X$. Tensoring with one such term commutes with products: for a free term the comparison is the coordinatewise identity $(\prod_m F_m)^N=\prod_m F_m^N$, and restriction to the images of the same idempotent gives the retract case. Boundedness of $E$ makes every diagonal of the total tensor a finite sum, so this proves the chain isomorphism $(\prod_m M_m)\otimes E\cong\prod_m(M_m\otimes E)$ for arbitrary complexes $M_m$. A bounded complex of these flat terms is K-flat: filter it by its finitely many degrees; tensoring an acyclic complex gives acyclic successive quotients, hence an acyclic total complex. Countable products are exact by [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact], and termwise products represent derived products by [lem-weil-derived-limit-products-core]. Thus the displayed chain identity computes the derived product comparison, even if the $M_m$ and $C$ are unbounded. It commutes with $1-s$ since each projection is the tensor of the corresponding projection and the transition is tensored with $1_E$. Tensor also commutes with the two finite summands and the differential of a mapping cone. Consequently the specified product-cone model satisfies $(R\lim M_m)\otimes^L(P_a)_X\cong R\lim(M_m\otimes^L(P_a)_X)$.

source.place: Proof, second and last sentences: explicit bounded finite-projective product calculation

proof.text: Apply step 2 to $M_m=C\otimes(Q_m)_X$. The total tensor model [def-weil-derived-tensor] identifies its reduced tower with $C\otimes((Q_m)_X\otimes(P_a)_X)$: $C$ is K-flat and $Q_m$ is bounded finite free, so replacing $E$ by $(P_a)_X$ here is a quasi-isomorphism (its cone is $C$ tensored with the bounded finite-free tensor of the acyclic cone of $E\to(P_a)_X$). The tensor reassociation sends $(c\otimes q)\otimes z$ to $c\otimes(q\otimes z)$ and respects the total differential. Discard levels $m<a$. This does not change the product-cone limit: the kernel of the projection from the full product to the tail product is the finite product of the removed levels, and $s$ on this kernel is strictly triangular with $s^{a-1}=0$; thus $1-s$ has inverse $1+s+\cdots+s^{a-2}$, and its cone is contractible. For $a=1$ nothing is removed.

source.place: Proof, reduction to m at least a, and the tensor model

proof.text: For $m\geq a$, every $f_j^m$ is zero in $P_a$, so the Koszul differential in $Q_m\otimes P_a$ is zero. Its degree $-d$ summands are copies of $P_a$ indexed by subsets $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}$ of size $d$. By the explicit transitions of [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-koszul-completion], the map over $a$ successive levels on the $J$-summand is multiplication by $\prod_{j\in J}f_j^a$. For $d>0$ this is zero because any one factor belongs to $I^a$. For $d=0$ it is the identity. Therefore, after tensoring with $C$, the tail tower splits as the constant tower $C\otimes(P_a)_X$ in Koszul degree zero plus a finite sum of shifted towers whose transition over $a$ levels is zero as a chain map. There are no cross differentials between these summands, since the Koszul differential is zero.

source.place: Proof, zero differentials and the explicit a-fold transition

proof.text: The negative-degree summand towers of step 4 have zero derived inverse limit by the pro-zero clause of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. For the constant tower on $N=C\otimes(P_a)_X$, the product map is $(x_m)\mapsto(x_m-x_{m+1})$; its kernel is the diagonal copy of $N$ and it is split surjective, with section $y\mapsto x$ defined by $x_a=0$ and $x_{m+1}=x_m-y_m$. These finite sums commute with the differential. Its product-cone fibre is therefore $N$, with evaluation equal to the identity under this identification. Finite direct sums commute with the product-cone formula, so the entire reduced Koszul tower has limit $N$, via its degree-zero augmentation. Together with steps 1–3 this proves an isomorphism $L\otimes^L(P_a)_X\to K_a$.

source.place: Proof, pro-zero towers and the constant degree-zero tower

proof.text: For clarity, the adjunction used here is supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction] for the identity topos morphism with ring map $\Lambda_X\to(P_a)_X$, and by [lem-pc-derived-adjoint-functors] after derivation. Restriction is exact because it leaves the underlying module sheaves and kernels/cokernels unchanged, so its termwise functor is its right derived functor. The everywhere-defined left derived extension is [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. It remains to identify the map. The comparison $c_K$ of [lemma-weil-pbc-koszul-quotient-limit] is induced by $Q_m\to P_m$. At level $a$, the adjoint of the composite $R\lim(C\otimes Q_m)\to C\otimes Q_a\to C\otimes P_a$ is evaluation after tensor with $P_a$, followed by the augmentation and multiplication $Q_a\otimes^L P_a\to P_a\otimes^L P_a\to P_a$. On the K-flat model this composite is $c\otimes q\otimes z\mapsto c\otimes\overline q z$ in Koszul degree zero and zero in negative Koszul degrees. This is exactly the degree-zero augmentation used in step 5. Hence the isomorphism constructed there is the adjoint of $p_a$, as defined by derived change of rings [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. All the maps used are induced by products, strict tower maps, tensor comparisons and augmentations; their formulas commute with maps of $C$. They consequently descend through K-flat resolutions to the natural transformations in the derived categories, proving functoriality in $K$. The computation in steps 2–5 takes place after restriction to $\Lambda_X$. Restriction reflects isomorphisms in the derived categories: it is exact and faithful on module sheaves, and the cohomology sheaves of the cone of a restricted morphism are the restrictions of the cohomology sheaves of its cone. Their vanishing therefore implies the original cone is acyclic. The identified adjoint is consequently an isomorphism in $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},P_a)$ itself.

source.place: Proof, surviving degree-zero projection is the displayed map
